resolutions.researcher_notes: Status='operating' confirmed by two independent sources naming the pipeline directly: GlobalData's profile states it started operations in 2019, and a 2020 Reuters/PGJ wire confirms it was an active, flowing pipeline (returning to service after maintenance) more than a year later — consistent with a durable 'operating' status, not a one-time startup event.

verifications.note: GlobalData profile breaks the line down into "264 km of 36-inch diameter and 10 km of 29-inch diameter" pipe — an exact match to the recorded Diameter='29, 36' in.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Diameter='29, 36' in is stated exactly (264 km @ 36-in + 10 km @ 29-in) by NS Energy Business/GlobalData, but this is a SINGLE source for the 29-in figure specifically -- searched for a second independent confirmation and did not find one: (1) the FERC certificate order (already opened/cited on this row) itemizes only 36-in (MXP-100 mainline, 164.5 mi), 24-in (MXP-200 Sherwood Lateral, 6.0 mi) and 30-in (SM-80 replacement, 0.4 mi) segments -- it corroborates the 36-in mainline diameter but names no 29-in segment anywhere in the document; (2) Alpha Three, Yahoo Finance/Reuters, and offshore-technology.com's own article text each cite only the 36-in mainline diameter, with no mention of a secondary 29-in run; (3) attempted a live web search for a corroborating source but this session's web-search budget was already exhausted; (4) attempted to reach S&P Global Platts' partial-service article (spglobal.com, already known to be relevant to this pipeline) directly via curl with a browser user-agent and via WebFetch -- both returned a genuine Akamai/edgesuite 403 Access Denied, not a content match; (5) attempted an Internet Archive Wayback lookup for a cached copy of that page and for a second capture of the nsenergybusiness page itself -- archive.org's availability API returned HTTP 429 on every retry across this session, a persistent rate-limit rather than a one-off. Leaving this as a single-sourced REFS_ADDED at medium tier rather than UNRESOLVED, since one verified source does state the exact recorded value and names the pipeline directly.

verifications.note: "With a project value of approximately $3.2 billion, the project can transport 2.7 billion cubic feet per day..." — states a total project cost of $3.2 billion.
Reuters/Yahoo Finance: final project cost of "$3.2 billion (including cost overruns; originally budgeted at $2.6 billion)" — an independent source agreeing with Alpha Three's $3.2 billion figure.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources agree with each other on a final project cost of $3.2 billion, against the recorded SegmentCost=$3,030,000,000 (3.03 billion USD) -- a ~5.6% ($170M) gap, larger than a simple rounding difference. FLAGGING FOR VALIDITY/ORCHESTRATOR: this may reflect a cost-overrun timeline issue -- FERC's original Dec. 2017 certificate order (already opened on this row) put Columbia Gas's own initial estimate at only $2.059 billion for the Mountaineer XPress facilities alone (excluding the companion Gulf XPress project's separate $674.3 million), while Yahoo/Reuters explicitly describes $3.2B as the FINAL cost after overruns from an original $2.6B budget. The recorded $3.03B sits between the original FERC estimate and the final overrun figure reported by both later sources, so it is plausibly an intermediate or partial (MXP-only, pre-final-overrun) estimate rather than an error, but it does not exactly match any single sourced figure -- recommend a human check whether $3.03B vs $3.2B is a genuine value correction or an acceptable variance before treating this as fully reconciled.
